Tarutyne Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Tarutyne, Ukraine

Not demolished. Established no later than 1875 per its oldest found gravestone, this cemetery appears on the town's Yizkor memory map; per Holocaust survivor testimonies published in Yizkor Tarutyne, it was totally destroyed during WWII and plowed under by tractors, with some matzevot later found in local house courtyards - however, the ESJF's own field survey found the cemetery still existing and comparatively well-preserved, a notable discrepancy from the survivors' account. Jewish settlement in Tarutyne, southern Bessarabia's second-largest Jewish community, dates to 1832; three synagogues operated by the late 19th century, and from the community's 1917 founding, Zionist views flourished alongside self-defense detachments, with about 60 youth emigrating to Palestine in the interwar period. Population reached 1,546 (27%) by 1930. German-Romanian occupation from July 1941 murdered about 40 Jews that month; an August 7 camp held 1,200 Jews, followed by an October 10 ghetto for 2,270 Jews from Izmail, Bolhrad, Kiliya, and Vylkove, deported to Transnistria October 25-27, 1941.
